top_story: A fragile Iran-US ceasefire is being tested on two linked fronts: maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz and Israeli escalation in Lebanon. After Iran briefly reopened the strait, the reported IRGC attack on a tanker and the confirmed assault on two Indian-flagged crude carriers on 18 April pushed Tehran back to threatening closure unless the United States lifts its blockade, despite later claims that passage had been restored under ceasefire terms. In Lebanon, tens of thousands of civilians returned to the south despite Israeli warnings, underscoring how ceasefire arrangements are colliding with immediate human need after deadly strikes near Sour. The regional picture is one of a highly unstable truce in which coercive signaling by states is already disrupting shipping, exposing foreign commercial actors, and forcing civilians to absorb the risks of unresolved escalation.
